cards.info: What is the definition of an independent variable in an experiment?
cards.backInfo: The factor that a researcher intentionally changes, varies, or assigns across different groups or trials.

cards.info: What is the definition of a dependent variable?
cards.backInfo: The outcome, response, or measurement recorded to assess the effect of the independent variable.

cards.info: How do you identify the independent variable in an experimental description?
cards.backInfo: Look for the factor that is varied or different between the experimental groups.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flow chart showing the process of identifying variables: Change leads to Independent Variable, and Measure leads to Dependent Variable.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/599623c3-8852-4614-9c60-9cf4c689dff4-1786506615929-122.webp)

cards.info: How do you identify the dependent variable in a trial?
cards.backInfo: Look for the specific quantity or observation the researcher records at the end.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flow chart showing the process of identifying variables: Change leads to Independent Variable, and Measure leads to Dependent Variable.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/599623c3-8852-4614-9c60-9cf4c689dff4-1786506615929-122.webp)

cards.info: On which axis is the independent variable typically plotted?
cards.backInfo: The independent variable is typically represented on the horizontal x-axis.

cards.info: On which axis is the dependent variable typically plotted?
cards.backInfo: The dependent variable is typically represented on the vertical y-axis.

cards.info: Where is the independent variable usually located in a data table?
cards.backInfo: The independent variable is usually located in the leftmost column of the table.

cards.info: What is a common mistake when identifying the independent variable?
cards.backInfo: Misidentifying a constant—a factor held the same across all groups—as the variable.

cards.info: In a cause-and-effect relationship, which variable acts as the 'cause'?
cards.backInfo: The independent variable acts as the 'cause,' while the dependent variable is the 'effect.'

cards.info: Which keywords signal the presence of an independent variable?
cards.backInfo: Keywords such as 'varied,' 'different,' or 'adjusted' often signal the independent variable.

cards.info: In the 'Change-to-Measure Mapping' strategy, what does the 'Change' represent?
cards.backInfo: The 'Change' represents the Independent Variable, which is the factor intentionally varied by the researcher.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flow chart showing the process of identifying variables: Change leads to Independent Variable, and Measure leads to Dependent Variable.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/599623c3-8852-4614-9c60-9cf4c689dff4-1786506615929-122.webp)

cards.info: In the 'Change-to-Measure Mapping' strategy, what does the 'Measure' represent?
cards.backInfo: The 'Measure' represents the Dependent Variable, which is the outcome or result recorded by the researcher.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flow chart showing the process of identifying variables: Change leads to Independent Variable, and Measure leads to Dependent Variable.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/599623c3-8852-4614-9c60-9cf4c689dff4-1786506615929-122.webp)

cards.info: If a passage says 'different dosages were assigned,' what is the independent variable?
cards.backInfo: The dosage is the independent variable because it is the factor varied between groups.

cards.info: If a passage says 'the time was recorded,' what is the dependent variable?
cards.backInfo: Time is the dependent variable because it is the specific observation recorded at the end.

cards.info: Which variable is typically found on the horizontal axis of an ACT graph?
cards.backInfo: The independent variable is typically found on the horizontal x-axis.

cards.info: Which variable is typically found on the vertical axis of an ACT graph?
cards.backInfo: The dependent variable is typically found on the vertical y-axis.

cards.info: In a table, where are the results (dependent variables) usually located?
cards.backInfo: The dependent variables usually occupy the columns to the right of the leftmost column.

cards.info: Why is '100 mL of water' in every beaker not a variable?
cards.backInfo: It is a constant, not a variable, because it is held the same across all groups.

cards.info: How can you verify if a factor is the dependent variable?
cards.backInfo: Check if the value was 'measured' or 'observed' rather than 'chosen' by the researcher.

cards.info: If a question asks for the 'effect of X on Y,' what is Y?
cards.backInfo: Y is the dependent variable (the effect), while X is the independent variable (the cause).
